[RFCS.7.3] A reader must treat a `FactRetract` as a fatal stream error
unless its `fact_id` is carried by a `FactAssert`, a `FactEmit` or one of an
`ExternalAssert`'s `fact_ids` ([RFCS.24.1]) earlier in the current file, whose
fact was in working memory when the reader met that atom, and no earlier
`FactRetract` named it. A runtime replaying the
stream must stop at that atom and return `DS_ERR_FS_UNKNOWN_FACT_ID`, the same
code whether it meets the atom as it opens the stream or partway through the
replay.

The integrator may retract a fact a rule emitted — a handle is a handle,
and nothing in the API distinguishes them — so the referent set is every
fact-bearing atom rather than only the integrator's. A well-formed recording
never holds a retract this clause refuses: the host had no live fact to
retract.
